children: Shares of recreational products manufacturer American Outdoor Brands

jumped 41.9% in the afternoon session after the company reported first-quarter fiscal 2027 financial results that exceeded Wall Street expectations for both revenue and profitability. According to the company's press release, American Outdoor Brands generated net sales of $37.25 million, representing a 25.4% increase compared to the prior-year period. On a non-GAAP basis, the outdoor product manufacturer reported net income of $415,000, or $0.03 per diluted share, which comfortably beat consensus analyst estimates of a $0.24 loss per share, according to FactSet.

The company also generated non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA of $1.16 million, or 3.1% of net sales, turning positive from negative $3.1 million in the same quarter last year, the release said. Driven by this momentum, management reconfirmed its full-year fiscal 2027 net sales guidance of $200 million to $210 million while raising its Adjusted EBITDA guidance range to between $14.5 million and $17.5 million. Additionally, the company's gross margin expanded by 630 basis points to 53.0% from 46.7% last year, supported by new product introductions, pricing actions, and favorable channel mix, according to its quarterly SEC filing.
What Is The Market Telling Us

American Outdoor Brands’s shares are very volatile and have had 21 moves greater than 5% over the last year. But moves this big are rare even for American Outdoor Brands and indicate this news significantly impacted the market’s perception of the business.

The biggest move we wrote about over the last year was 2 months ago when the stock gained 18.9% on the news that the company reported first-quarter results where a significant profit beat overshadowed a miss on revenue and guidance that was slightly below expectations. Adjusted earnings per share for the quarter came in at $0.13, substantially better than the analyst consensus of a $0.01 loss.

This strong bottom-line performance, along with adjusted EBITDA that was more than double the Wall Street consensus, appeared to capture investor attention. While quarterly revenue of $47.06 million fell 24% year-over-year and missed expectations, the market focused on the company's profitability. Looking ahead, the company's full-year revenue guidance, with a midpoint of $205 million, was also slightly below analysts' projections. The company ended the quarter with $21.44 million in cash and $32.38 million of debt.

American Outdoor Brands is up 77.7% since the beginning of the year, and at $14.08 per share, it is trading close to its 52-week high of $14.49 from July 2026. Despite the year-to-date gain, investors who bought $1,000 worth of American Outdoor Brands’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at only $548.52.
